package_info.why_malicious: The flatmap-stream package was intentionally modified to include obfuscated, crypto-stealing malicious code. This code was designed to activate only in specific application contexts (notably, the copay-dash wallet app), exfiltrating sensitive wallet data to an attacker-controlled server. The package was then added as a dependency to the widely used event-stream package, resulting in a large-scale supply chain attack that propagated the malicious payload to numerous downstream projects and even VS Code extensions, putting developer credentials and assets at risk.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when the package is required or executed in a Node.js process, specifically within targeted applications such as copay-dash)
execution_context.file_location: flatmap-stream/index.js (main entry point, containing obfuscated payload)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the package is loaded within a targeted application (such as copay-dash), the code checks the environment, reads sensitive wallet data from the filesystem, and sends this data via HTTP POST to a hardcoded malicious domain, resulting in the exfiltration of private keys and user assets.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code is obfuscated and conditionally executes only when running inside a specific application, accesses sensitive wallet files, and exfiltrates their contents to an external server. This targeted, stealthy behavior is characteristic of supply chain attacks aiming to steal high-value credentials.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages should not contain hidden or obfuscated payloads that activate only in certain environments, nor should they access or transmit sensitive user data such as wallet files without explicit user consent. Normal dependencies do not perform targeted data exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate telemetry or crash reporting may send anonymized, non-sensitive data to a vendor's server, but never private keys, wallet files, or other confidential user assets. Such reporting is also never obfuscated or hidden within a dependency.
key_indicators: Obfuscated or minified code in a dependency with low prior usage
Conditional execution based on environment variables or package name (e.g., process.env.npm_package_name === 'copay-dash')
Access to sensitive files such as wallet.dat or private keys
Outbound HTTP POST requests to hardcoded, suspicious domains from within a package dependency
Presence of hidden payloads in the main entry point of a dependency

attack_chain.action: Malicious, obfuscated code is added to flatmap-stream and published to npm.
attack_chain.leads_to: Inclusion as a dependency in the event-stream package.

attack_chain.action: event-stream package (v3.3.6) is updated to depend on the malicious flatmap-stream version.
attack_chain.leads_to: Propagation to all projects and packages using event-stream@3.x.x.

attack_chain.action: Downstream npm packages and VS Code extensions include event-stream@3.x.x as a dependency, unknowingly pulling in flatmap-stream.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is included in VS Code extensions and other projects.

attack_chain.action: VS Code extensions are auto-updated on developer machines, bringing in the malicious dependency chain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present and ready to execute on developer systems at next VS Code startup.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes in the context of the developer's environment, conditionally targeting specific applications (e.g., copay-dash) and exfiltrating sensitive data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromise of developer credentials, wallet files, and other sensitive assets.

behavioral_signatures: Conditional execution of code based on environment variables or package name (e.g., process.env.npm_package_name === 'copay-dash')
Access to sensitive files such as wallet.dat, private keys, or cryptocurrency wallet data within Node.js dependencies
Outbound HTTP or HTTPS POST requests to hardcoded or previously unknown domains from package dependencies
Obfuscated or minified code present in dependencies with low download counts or recent, unexplained updates
file_indicators: flatmap-stream/index.js containing obfuscated or suspicious code
event-stream/package.json listing flatmap-stream as a dependency
VS Code extensions or npm projects with flatmap-stream or event-stream@3.x.x in their dependency tree
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to domains such as malicious-domain.com from developer or build environments
Network connections initiated by Node.js processes during package installation or runtime to unknown or suspicious endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the presence of flatmap-stream or event-stream@3.x.x in the dependency trees of Node.js projects and VS Code extensions. Use static analysis to scan for obfuscated or minified code in flatmap-stream/index.js, especially code that conditionally executes based on environment variables or package names. Flag any code that accesses wallet.dat or other sensitive files and attempts outbound network connections to hardcoded domains. Correlate network telemetry to detect HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to suspicious domains from development or CI environments, particularly during package installation or extension updates.
